facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus was described by Larsson and Gado in 2000.
facts.quote: authority: Larsson and Gado, 2000

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: Fossils of Stolokrosuchus have been found in the Lower Cretaceous Elrhaz Formation in Niger.
facts.quote: found in the Lower Cretaceous Elrhaz Formation, Niger

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus is known from a nearly complete skull with a narrow, highly elongated, and tubular snout resembling modern gharials.
facts.quote: It is known from a nearly complete skull displaying a narrow, highly elongated and tubular snout similar to modern gharials

facts.statement: While some studies place Stolokrosuchus within the Notosuchia, others propose a closer relationship to Neosuchia.
facts.quote: While all of these placements would classify Stolokrosuchus as a notosuchian, other studies have proposed a closer relationship to Neosuchia

facts.statement: The fossils of Stolokrosuchus come from the GAD 5 site in the Aptian to Albian Elrhaz Formation in Niger.
facts.quote: The fossils come from the GAD 5 site of the Aptian to Albian Elrhaz Formation in Niger

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus preserves a small, slit-like antorbital fenestra primarily formed by the lacrimal bone.
facts.quote: Stolokrosuchus preserves a small, slit-like antorbital fenestra that is primarily formed by the lacrimal

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus lacks the subtympanic foramen, a feature shared with modern gharials and Pepesuchus but absent in other extant crocodilians.
facts.quote: both Stolokrosuchus and Pepesuchus lack the subtympanic foramen like is also the case in modern gharials but not in other extant crocodilians

facts.statement: The quadrate bone of Stolokrosuchus has two elongated crests, labeled A and B, which served as attachment points for adductor muscles.
facts.quote: The ventral surface of the quadrate bears two elongated crests regarded to be attachment sites for the adductor musculature, designated crests A and B.

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus had a narrow, flattened lower jaw joint formed by dentary and splenial bones meeting at a V-shaped suture.
facts.quote: The flattened mandibular symphysis of Stolokrosuchus is narrow to match the narrow elongated rostrum, lacks a constriction and is formed by both the dentary bones and the splenials, which meet along a V-shaped suture.

facts.statement: The splenial bone contributed approximately 25% to 30% of the total width of the lower jaw ramus in Stolokrosuchus.
facts.quote: The splenial's contribution to the width of the mandibular ramus is comparable to taxa like Gasparinisuchus and Barrosasuchus, making up about 25-30 % of the mandible's entire mediolateral width.

facts.statement: Unlike most peirosaurids, the top surface of the lower jaw in Stolokrosuchus was straight instead of having a wavy profile.
facts.quote: The dorsal surface of the mandible is straight rather than festooned, meaning that the lower jaw of Stolokrosuchus lacked the wave-like or sinusoidal profile seen in most peirosaurids.

facts.statement: Each side of the upper jaw of Stolokrosuchus contained 30 teeth, consisting of 5 in the premaxilla and 25 in the maxilla.
facts.quote: The upper jaw of Stolokrosuchus contains a total of 30 teeth on either side, 5 in each premaxilla and an additional 25 in each maxilla.

facts.statement: The maxillary teeth in Stolokrosuchus reached their largest size at the fifth and thirteenth positions along the jaw.
facts.quote: The first two teeth of the maxilla project slightly forward and after this point the toothrow exhibits slight festooning, with the maxillary teeth reaching their greatest size with the fifth and 13th teeth.

facts.statement: In Stolokrosuchus, the first tooth of the lower jaw was the largest, contrasting with most other peirosaurids where the fourth tooth is largest.
facts.quote: While in most other peirosaurids the fourth dentary tooth is the largest in the mandible, in Stolokrosuchus the first dentary tooth is the largest.

facts.statement: The cutting edges of Stolokrosuchus teeth were smooth and lacked serrations or crenulations, similar to the possibly related Epoidesuchus.
facts.quote: Like in the possibly related Epoidesuchus the carinae or cutting edges of Stolokrosuchus teeth are smooth and bear neither crenulations nor serrations as is frequently the case in both itasuchids and peirosaurids.

facts.statement: Researcher France de Lapparent de Broin suggested that the fourth and fifteenth lower jaw teeth of Stolokrosuchus may have interlocked with the upper jaw teeth.
facts.quote: France de Lapparent de Broin has suggested that the fourth and 15th dentary teeth may have interlocked with the dentition of the upper jaw while other parts of the toothrow show an overbite.

facts.statement: The skull of Stolokrosuchus was 481 mm long, and the animal is estimated to have weighed around 230 kg.
facts.quote: The skull of Stolokrosuchus measures 481 mm in length and the animal may have weighed around 230 kg based on calculations by Bravo and colleagues.

facts.statement: Larsson and Gado originally classified Stolokrosuchus as a peirosaurid closely related to Peirosaurus and Lomasuchus.
facts.quote: Larsson and Gado initially described Stolokrosuchus as a member of the Peirosauridae in an unresolved sister taxon relationship with Peirosaurus and Lomasuchus.

facts.statement: A 2014 study by Sertich and colleagues placed Stolokrosuchus within Peirosauridae as a derived member related to African forms like Rukwasuchus and Hamadasuchus.
facts.quote: In 2014 Sertich and colleagues also recovered Stolokrosuchus as a peirosaurid, specifically as a derived member closely related to other African forms like Rukwasuchus and Hamadasuchus.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that Stolokrosuchus may belong to families other than Peirosauridae within Notosuchia.
facts.quote: Other studies meanwhile have suggested that Stolokrosuchus, while nonetheless close to peirosaurids, might be better placed in other families within Notosuchia.

facts.statement: A 2012 study by Bronzati and colleagues found Stolokrosuchus closely related to peirosaurids, mahajangasuchids, and Trematochampsidae, but placed this group outside Notosuchia as basal to Neosuchia.
facts.quote: In a 2012 study Bronzati and colleagues regarded Stolokrosuchus with close affinities to not just peirosaurids but also mahajangasuchids and the now dubious clade Trematochampsidae, though their study did not place this grouping within Notosuchia but as a clade basal to Neosuchia.

facts.statement: Pinheiro and colleagues in 2023 included Stolokrosuchus within the family Itasuchidae as the most basal member.
facts.quote: In a 2023 paper describing additional material for multiple itasuchids Pinheiro and colleagues managed to recover a similar topology, but now included Stolokrosuchus as the basalmost itasuchid and included it in the clades definition.

facts.statement: France de Lapparent de Broin classified Stolokrosuchus in the family Elosuchidae in 2002 based on features hypothesized to be shared with Elosuchus.
facts.quote: In 2002 France de Lapparent de Broin placed Stolokrosuchus in the newly established family Elosuchidae alongside the eponymous genus Elosuchus, a longirostrine genus from the Cretaceous of Africa, based on a variety of features often only hypothesized for Stolokrosuchus or stated to be "possibly shared".

facts.statement: Andrade and colleagues in 2011 recovered Stolokrosuchus as a basal offshoot of a clade containing goniopholidids, elosuchids, and marine thalattosuchians.
facts.quote: In 2011 Andrade and colleagues proposed a new definition of Elosuchidae and instead recovered Stolokrosuchus as a basal offshoot of a clade that includes goniopholidids, elosuchids (including Sarcosuchus) and the marine thalattosuchians.

facts.statement: Sertich and colleagues in 2014 argued that previous classifications placing Stolokrosuchus as a neosuchian might be due to missing holotype material and convergent evolution of its skull shape.
facts.quote: Despite recovering Stolokrosuchus as a neosuchian in prior studies, by 2014 Sertich and colleagues argue that this pattern may be due to the absence of important parts of the palate in the holotype as well as the convergently evolved longirostrine skull form.

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus is considered semi-aquatic due to its long, tubular snout and eyes positioned on the top of its head.
facts.quote: Stolokrosuchus is frequently regarded as a semi-aquatic taxon on account of features such its longirostrine tubular snout and more dorsally oriented eyes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Stolokrosuchus likely fed on agile prey like fish using its long and narrow jaws.
facts.quote: With its long and narrow jaws it might have fed on agile prey such as fish.

facts.statement: The only known fossils of Stolokrosuchus were found in the Elrhaz Formation in present-day Niger.
facts.quote: The only known remains of Stolokrosuchus come from Gadoufaoua, specifically deposits belonging of the Aptian to Albian Elrhaz Formation (upper Tegama Group) in what is now Niger.

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus belongs to the parent group Peirosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Peirosauridae

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus is classified within the family Peirosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Peirosauridae

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Stolokrosuchus lived between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago during the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Stolokrosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
